youtube_description:
Ever cried yourself to sleep and wondered if anyone noticed? Psalm 6 is David's raw, honest prayer, and it ends with his tears heard.

In verse 3 David cries out, "And you, O LORD, how long?" The Hebrew is 'ad-matay (ahd-mah-TIE), literally "until when?", and the sentence breaks off unfinished. A few verses later: "The LORD has heard the sound of my weeping" (Psalm 6:8-9).

Today's step: tonight, if the words won't come, give God the half sentence. Give him the tears.

Day 6 of the Psalms, one chapter a day. Follow @thebibleexplainedai so you don't miss Psalm 7.

Read it: Psalm 6:1-10

#Psalm6 #BibleStudy #Bible #Prayer #Shorts

Ever cried yourself to sleep and wondered if anyone noticed? 💧 Psalm 6 says the sound of your weeping reaches God.

David floods his bed with tears every night. Then, near the end, everything turns: "The LORD has heard the sound of my weeping." (Psalm 6:8)

In verse 3 he can't even finish his sentence: "And you, O LORD, how long?" The Hebrew, 'ad-matay, literally means "until when?"

Tonight, if the words won't come, give God the half sentence.

🔖 Save this for a hard night
💬 What's your "how long?" right now? We'll pray for you.
